_note: Runtime LLM selection overrides (issue #11). Copy to llm_config.json in this
same directory to activate. llm_config.json is git-tracked (not gitignored —
it's a deliberate configuration decision, not machine-written ephemeral state,
so it gets the same audit trail as everything else); edits still take effect
on the next run without a code change, PR or review — that's a property of
the loader re-reading the file, unrelated to whether git tracks it.
Anything omitted falls back to the built-in defaults in scripts/llm_config.py,
which are also what this file reproduces verbatim. Invalid values fall back
per field, not per file. Every effective override is logged at INFO on load
('LLM config override: <stage>.<field>: old -> new'), so grep the run log to
confirm a change took effect: /tmp/daily_intelligence.log (reports) or
/tmp/finance_telegram.log (bot).
Report scripts re-read this file on every launchd run. The Telegram bot
re-reads it when its mtime changes, so no restart is needed for config-only
edits (code changes still require one, see docs/PITFALLS.md#32).
Field notes: 'model'/'fallback_model' must be OpenRouter slugs ('vendor/model',
optionally '~vendor/model-latest'). 'providers' is OpenRouter's provider
routing object, or null for no pin. 'thinking' applies to the primary model;
'fallback_reasoning' is OpenRouter's unified reasoning-effort param applied to
the fallback model. Keys starting with '_' are ignored (JSON has no comments).
